pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text:
`vega_pnl_attribution` answers "how much P&L came from a move in volatility?" It multiplies portfolio vega (`vega`) by the realised volatility move (`vol_move`), giving one component of a P&L explanation.

`pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` answers a different question: "does my model-based P&L track the full-revaluation P&L well enough?" It takes two daily series, `risk_theoretical_pnl` and `hypothetical_pnl`. It evaluates their Spearman rank correlation together with the ratio of their standard deviations, then assigns a Basel traffic-light zone. The thresholds are set by the Basel Committee and are not parameters you can change.

So the first explains a source of P&L, while the second tests the quality of a model's P&L as a whole.

explain.text: `vega_pnl_attribution` (Vega Pnl Attribution) computes the vega component of a portfolio's P&L, which is the portfolio's vega multiplied by a volatility move: ν · dσ. You supply two inputs: `vega`, the portfolio's sensitivity of value to volatility (∂V/∂σ), and `vol_move`, the realised volatility move dσ. The function returns the P&L attributed to that volatility change. In a P&L explain, this is the piece that isolates how much of the result comes from volatility moving, separate from other risk factors.

when.text:
`vega_pnl_attribution` fits when you want the volatility part of a portfolio's P&L, calculated as vega times the realised volatility move (`vega` × `vol_move`).

- You already have the portfolio vega (∂V/∂σ) and a realised volatility move dσ, and want to see how much P&L that move accounts for.
- You're breaking a P&L explain into Greek components and need the vega piece on its own.
- You want a simple first-order link between a change in volatility and its P&L effect, as part of market risk reporting.
- For gamma, the related function `gamma_pnl_attribution` covers the convexity component, listed as ½ · Γ · dS².
